population: Unselected (mild-to-moderate AD; early amyloid-positive AD for lecanemab)
note: Antibodies to amyloid-β (ponezumab, crenezumab, lecanemab), each tested first in APP-overexpressing mice.
label: Alzheimer's (anti-Aβ mAbs)

engagement.model: Aged APP transgenic mice given 2H6, ponezumab's murine parent
engagement.note: Weekly 2H6 for 4 months cut brain amyloid in 20-month-old APP mice.
engagement.quote: Both groups receiving anti-Abeta antibodies showed significant reductions in total Abeta immunochemistry and Congo red.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the first published in-vivo model behind a member (ponezumab = humanized 2H6).

engagement.magnitude_basis: brain amyloid: significant fall in mice vs no change on PIB-PET in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). registry_date assumes this study is NCT00945672 (multiple-dose ponezumab, Sweden); not confirmed from the paper.
engagement.model: Aged APP transgenic mice given 2H6, ponezumab's murine parent
engagement.note: Ponezumab for a year raised plasma Aβ but left brain amyloid on PIB-PET unchanged.
engagement.quote: Plasma Aβ increased dose dependently with ponezumab, but CSF biomarkers, brain amyloid burden, cognition, and function were not affected.
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: Wilcock's brain-amyloid readout set against the PIB-PET substudy. Plaque is the aggregated product of the target, so proximal. Crenezumab's BLAZE PET (Salloway 2018) also showed no significant amyloid fall.

engagement.model_filed: BLA 761269 pharmacology review, Study AD-TR-007: 18 weeks of mAb158 cut brain protofibrils 80% with no change in insoluble Aβ or plaques
engagement.magnitude_basis: insoluble Aβ/plaque: no change in plaque-bearing tg-ArcSwe mice vs -0.306 SUVr in patients
engagement.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). FDA review read in full from the source bundle.
engagement.model: tg-ArcSwe mice given mAb158, lecanemab's murine version
engagement.note: mAb158 lowered protofibrils but not plaque in plaque-bearing mice; lecanemab cut amyloid PET in patients.
engagement.short: Mice: no plaque fall; patients: PET fell
engagement.quote: At 18 months, 10-mg/kg biweekly lecanemab reduced brain amyloid (-0.306 SUVr units) while showing a drug-placebo difference in favor of active treatment by 27% and 30% on ADCOMS
engagement.reason: Model missed plaque clearance in patients
engagement.judgement: The model's main readout, brain protofibrils, was not measured in patients; scored on its secondary readout, insoluble Aβ, which the model said would not move and which fell. magnitude left null: model null vs a large patient effect is neither within-x nor opposite.

dose.model: hAPP(V717I)/PS1 mice and microglia assays with crenezumab
dose.note: Crenezumab cleared plaque on live imaging in hAPP/PS1 mice; no human exposure target was stated.
dose.short: Plaque cleared in mice; no exposure target
dose.quote: Furthermore, MABT-mediated amyloid plaque removal was demonstrated using in vivo live imaging in hAPP((V717I))/PS1 transgenic mice.
dose.judgement: Opened on crenezumab's model, the only member with a dose that failed and was then raised; no member published a model-derived human exposure target.

dose.magnitude_basis: no model exposure target to compare
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). Year from the July 2014 AC Immune release and AAIC presentation of ABBY (https://ir.acimmune.com/static-files/928e1976-2e72-4689-8a78-bfa462bbe368); ABBY (NCT01343966) has no posted registry results.
dose.model: hAPP(V717I)/PS1 mice and microglia assays with crenezumab
dose.note: 15 mg/kg crenezumab missed both primaries; sponsor moved to higher doses, which later failed in CREAD.
dose.short: 15 mg/kg failed; higher doses failed too
dose.quote: Together with the safety profile for crenezumab, these data support the exploration of crenezumab treatment at even higher doses in patients with early AD.
dose.judgement: Row 'reached, failed, abandoned': ABBY dosed as planned and failed; CREAD at 60 mg/kg stopped for futility in Jan 2019 (Genentech release; NCT02670083 results posted 2020-07-16), so the higher dose never worked. Low confidence because no model-stated exposure target exists.

efficacy.model: Aged APP transgenic mice given 2H6, ponezumab's murine parent
efficacy.note: 2H6 restored water-maze memory in aged APP mice.
efficacy.short: 2H6 restored maze memory in APP mice
efficacy.quote: APP transgenic mice receiving either anti-Abeta (2H6) or deglycosylated anti-Abeta (de-2H6) showed significant improvement in radial arm water maze performance compared with mice receiving a control antibody.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry on the earliest member model with a cognitive readout.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ADAS-Cog12 and CDR-SB change at week 73 vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). Year from the July 2014 AC Immune release/AAIC presentation; ABBY has no posted registry results.
efficacy.model: hAPP(V717I)/PS1 mice and microglia assays with crenezumab
efficacy.note: Mouse plaque clearance predicted benefit; crenezumab missed both ADAS-Cog12 and CDR-SB in ABBY.
efficacy.quote: The primary and secondary endpoints were not met.

patient_trials.quote: Ponezumab had no effects on cognitive/functional outcomes or brain volume.
Genentech to discontinue Phase III CREAD 1 and 2 clinical studies of crenezumab in early Alzheimer's disease (press release, 29 Jan 2019; title-level only)

efficacy.judgement: Adolfsson's model showed plaque removal, not cognition; scored as the class's efficacy prediction for crenezumab. Ponezumab's phase 2 had a safety primary, so it sits in patient_trials, not as the scoring entry.

efficacy.model_filed: BLA 761269 pharmacology review, Study W-20100159: mAb158 3-12 mg/kg for 18 weeks did not improve contextual or cued fear conditioning in APPArcSwe mice
efficacy.magnitude_basis: memory: no effect in mice vs 27% slowing of CDR-SB in patients
efficacy.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). Lord 2009 notes place learning depended on neither treatment nor transgenicity, so the mouse null may reflect an insensitive test.
efficacy.model: tg-ArcSwe mice given mAb158, lecanemab's murine version
efficacy.note: mAb158 gave the mice no memory benefit; lecanemab slowed CDR-SB decline 0.45 points in Clarity AD.
efficacy.short: Mice no benefit; Clarity AD positive
efficacy.quote: The adjusted least-squares mean change from baseline at 18 months was 1.21 with lecanemab and 1.66 with placebo (difference, -0.45; 95% CI, -0.67 to -0.23; P<0.001).
efficacy.reason: Lecanemab's mouse showed no benefit; drug worked

patient_trials.quote: BAN2401-G000-201 did not meet the 12-month primary endpoint.

efficacy.judgement: Scored the mouse's null behavioural result as a prediction of no benefit; low confidence because the tests may have had no deficit to rescue. Study 201 missed a Bayesian 80% gate at 12 months while favouring drug, then favoured drug at 18 months; not scored as agreeing with the mouse null.

safety.model: Aged APP transgenic mice given 2H6, ponezumab's murine parent
safety.note: Intact 2H6 raised microhemorrhage in APP mice; effector-reduced 2H6 largely did not.
safety.quote: Significantly fewer vascular amyloid deposits and microhemorrhages were observed in mice administered the de-2H6 antibody compared with those receiving unmodified 2H6 antibody.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: mice with vascular amyloid can show microhemorrhage, so the species could show the harm.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). Phase 1 numbers not given in the abstract; ABBY later reported one ARIA-E case in 431 patients.
safety.model: hAPP(V717I)/PS1 mice and microglia assays with crenezumab
safety.note: IgG4 crenezumab dampened microglial activation; phase 1 patients showed no vasogenic edema, even ApoE4 carriers.
safety.short: Low-effector IgG4: no edema in phase 1
safety.quote: Data from a phase I clinical trial testing MABT is consistent with this hypothesis, showing no signs of vasogenic edema, even in ApoE4 carriers.
safety.judgement: The prediction rests on in-vitro microglial assays (p38MAPK, TNFα), recorded as ex_vivo, the nearest model_kind; the source states the comparison itself.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract). Ponezumab's reduced effector function (engineered IgG2) taken from general knowledge, not re-read in a source.
safety.model: Aged APP transgenic mice given 2H6, ponezumab's murine parent
safety.note: Effector-attenuated ponezumab gave no excess microhemorrhage over 18 months versus placebo.
safety.quote: Most common adverse events were fall (16.7% ponezumab, 21.4% placebo), headache (13.8%, 21.4%), and cerebral microhemorrhage (13.8%, 19.6%).
safety.judgement: An in-vivo model taking over from crenezumab's in-vitro one (model_change). Lecanemab, a full-effector IgG1, gave ARIA-E 12.6% in Clarity AD, consistent with the same model, but no microhemorrhage model was run for it (FDA waived it in 2014), so it is not scored.
